key_insight: With an associated PDE discretized in time, the paper establishes Lipschitz stability and uniqueness for two 3D wave-equation coefficient inverse problems using data from a single point-source location.
engineering_relevance: The results support recovering spatially varying material parameters from wave measurements without requiring multiple source locations.
method: Recover an unknown potential in CIP1 and a principal-part coefficient in CIP2.
Use time finite differences in an associated PDE to establish stability and uniqueness.
Develop numerical methods with global convergence guarantees for both problems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive CIP1 numerical tests on complicated media with noisy data and consistently high accuracy, but provides no quantitative metrics.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on the stated time-discretized formulation, and the abstract reports computational validation only for CIP1.
paper_title: Two 3-Dimensional Coefficient Inverse Problems for Wave-like Equations With a Single Location of the Point Source
